claims: You don't need to build a model, just connect the right pieces (home, harness, model, memory, tools, interface)
VPS beats a home machine because it stays on 24/7 and is secure
Skills teach the agent to execute repeatable jobs per business role
how_to_steps: 1. Give it a home: VPS (or old computer / Mac mini)
3. Install/choose an AI model (Claude, ChatGPT, or open source)
4. Have Jarvis interview you about your business, life and goals
5. Give it persistent memory (AI second brain)
6. Create skills for each job role
9. Build an AI dashboard / command centre
on_screen_only: 'BUILD JARVIS STEP 01/09 ... 09/09' slide series with bullets: 'Always on. Always connected'; 'Plans the work / Uses tools and takes action / Checks its own results'; 'Reasoning and judgment / Code-heavy workflows / Long-context + multimodal -- SWAP THE BRAIN'; 'Your role, goals and priorities / Your business and workflows / Your rules and standards'; 'Remembers key decisions / Builds on past conversations / Gets smarter with use'; 'Teach one repeatable job / Package the workflow once / Stack skills into capability'; 'Email and calendar / Files and documents / Browser and business apps'; 'Chat from anywhere / Voice in real time / Alerts when work is done'; 'See goals and active tasks / Approve important actions / Review output and performance'
'Comment Jarvis for the full step by step guide'
cta: Comment 'Jarvis' to get the course/community link in bio

relevance.why: A sane high-level architecture that matches what the founder already does with Claude Code (skills, memory, MCP tools), but it is a funnel video with no concrete commands or repos beyond 'Hermes'.

implement_score.why: The checklist is useful to audit an existing Claude Code setup (memory, skills, channels, dashboard); building a separate always-on Jarvis on a VPS is a distraction unless there is a specific recurring job for it.
